title: Food miles distance table
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y5 lesson 17 (Food miles distance table (portal printable; approximate distances))
intro: Lesson 17: Food miles and trade. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.answers: Green beans: 6,850 km; Tomatoes: 1,750 km; Apples: 18,850 km; Potatoes: 200 km. Rank: New Zealand apples, Kenya beans, Spanish tomatoes, UK potatoes.

bullets: Longer journeys usually use more fuel
Planes use the most per kilogram

model.title: Green beans from Kenya to a London shop

parts.text: So about 6,850 km of food miles

panels.title: More than miles
points: Seasonal local food can use less

keywords.def: the distance food travels from farm to plate
trade that pays farmers a fair price

questions.q: Dates from Saudi Arabia travel about 4,900 km to London by air, plus 30 km by van. Total?
Why might a farmer abroad want fair trade?
questions.a: To get a fair price for their crops

questions.q: Name one local seasonal food in June.
Core: Use the distance table to work out the food miles for four foods (Kenya beans, Spanish tomatoes, New Zealand apples, UK potatoes) and rank them.
questions.a: Approximate distances ranked from longest (New Zealand) to shortest (UK)

questions.q: Extend: Write which food you would choose to cut food miles and why.
questions.a: For example: UK potatoes, because they travel only a short way

questions.q: Stretch: Why might food miles not tell the whole story?
questions.a: Heated greenhouses use energy; ships use little fuel; fair pay matters too

questions.q: Which transport uses the most fuel per kilogram?
questions.a: C) Plane. Planes are fastest but use far more fuel for each kilogram carried.

questions.q: Big question: Spanish tomato or English greenhouse tomato?
questions.a: It depends: Spain is further, but a heated greenhouse uses energy; seasonal local is often best
